steps.title: Welcome to agentgateway
steps.explanation:
agentgateway is the single control point every AI call in an organization can flow through - whether that's a chatbot answering a question or an AI agent calling a tool - instead of every team building its own access, safety, and cost controls against each AI provider separately.

- This wizard drives a live agentgateway: every step applies real configuration to a real cluster and sends real requests through it.
- You'll watch the gateway's policies actually working, not just read about them.

Here's what you'll see:

title: One endpoint, many models
teaser: Smart model routing with automatic fallback when a backend degrades.

steps.title: Model routing by name
steps.explanation:
Acme Corp's teams all call one agentgateway address, but each request can ask for a different AI model by name.

- Here, that's OpenAI's gpt-4o-mini or Anthropic's Claude.
- The gateway reads which model the request wants and forwards it to the right provider.
- One address, many models, and no routing logic in the app itself.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant OAI as OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini)
  participant ANT as Anthropic (Claude)
  Client->>AGW: POST /chat/by-name (X-Demo-Model: gpt-4o-mini)
  AGW->>OAI: forward
  OAI-->>Client: response
  Client->>AGW: POST /chat/by-name (X-Demo-Model: claude-sonnet-5)
  AGW->>ANT: forward
  ANT-->>Client: response

steps.title: Dynamic routing
steps.explanation:
The gateway doesn't have to route by model name - anything in the request can steer it.

- Here, a simple "tier" label on the request picks between a fast, cheap model and a premium one.
- The caller just asks for "fast" or "premium" and never needs to know which actual model sits behind each tier.
steps.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Client -->|"X-Model-Tier: fast"| AGW[agentgateway]
  Client -->|"X-Model-Tier: premium"| AGW
  AGW -->|fast| Fast[gpt-4o-mini]
  AGW -->|premium| Premium[gpt-4o]

steps.title: Automatic fallback
steps.explanation:
Real traffic has to keep working even when a provider is having a bad day.

- agentgateway ranks the AI providers in priority order.
- If the preferred one slows down or starts failing, traffic shifts to the next one automatically, in the moment.
- No retry code in the app, and no one paged to flip a switch by hand.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant Cheap as gpt-4o-mini (priority 100)
  participant Premium as gpt-4o (priority 50)
  Client->>AGW: request
  AGW->>Cheap: try priority 100 first
  Cheap-->>AGW: unhealthy / unavailable
  AGW->>Premium: fail over automatically
  Premium-->>Client: response

steps.title: Streaming responses
steps.explanation:
agentgateway speaks OpenAI's API natively, so streaming just works: adding "stream": true to the request is all it takes - there's no extra setting to turn on.

- The same by-name route from the first step now sends the answer back piece by piece, as the model writes it.
- The user starts reading right away instead of waiting for the whole reply to finish.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant OAI as OpenAI
  Client->>AGW: POST /chat/by-name (stream: true)
  AGW->>OAI: forward as-is
  OAI-->>AGW: SSE chunk 1
  AGW-->>Client: data: {...}
  OAI-->>AGW: SSE chunk 2
  AGW-->>Client: data: {...}
  OAI-->>AGW: data: [DONE]
  AGW-->>Client: data: [DONE]

title: Who's allowed to do what
teaser: Four questions every call must answer - enforced live on real banking agents and tools.

steps.title: Four questions every call must answer
steps.explanation:
Everything after this step is a real AI agent calling a real banking tool on your behalf. Before agentgateway lets any of those calls through, it checks the same four things every time - and logging in only settles the first two.

- **Question 1 - who is this for?** The call has to act for the real customer, not a stand-in (the identity in the token's `sub`).
- **Question 2 - who is actually doing it?** When one agent hands work to another, every agent in the chain is named, in order (the `act` chain).
- **Question 3 - is this token meant for this exact service?** Each time the gateway passes a token along, it narrows what that token is good for, so one stolen on its way to the ledger is useless anywhere else (the `aud`).
- **Question 4 - is this agent allowed to do this one thing, right now?** Decided at the moment of each tool call: the overlap between what the agent *can* do and what you actually asked it to do.

Logging in answers only the first two. agentgateway checks all four, on every single call.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Agent
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant MCP as Core Banking MCP
  You->>Agent: "Move $500 from savings to checking."
  Agent->>AGW: MCP tool call (Bearer JWT)
  Note over AGW: Question 1 (sub) - who is this on behalf of?
  Note over AGW: Question 2 (act / act.act) - who is actually acting?
  Note over AGW: Question 3 (aud) - is this token meant for this service?
  Note over AGW: Question 4 (per-tool authz) - capability ∩ delegated consent?
  AGW->>MCP: forward, only if all four pass
  MCP-->>You: result

steps.title: Real login
steps.explanation:
Every other step in this wizard takes a shortcut to log you in: the wizard itself asks Keycloak (the identity provider) for a token using a fixed demo username and password. That's fine for showing off routing or cost, but it's the wrong way to prove **Question 1** - who a real customer actually is.

This step does it properly, the way a real app would:

- agentgateway itself - not the wizard - sends you to Keycloak's own hosted login page, and you sign in there.
- From then on, every call in this pillar carries your real identity, attached by agentgateway as a standard login token - the wizard never handles it.
- agentgateway quietly renews that login in the background, so your session keeps working without anyone managing it.

It's the welcome screen's promise made literal: agentgateway is the one point every call flows through - and here, that includes the login itself, not just the banking calls that follow.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram participant Browser participant AGW as agentgateway (ext-auth) participant KC as Keycloak Browser->>AGW: GET /secure/login?returnTo=auth AGW->>AGW: no session yet AGW-->>Browser: 302 to Keycloak's real hosted login page Browser->>KC: log in as team-alpha or team-beta KC-->>AGW: authorization code AGW->>KC: exchange for tokens AGW->>AGW: bank session (Redis), set session cookie AGW-->>Browser: 302 back into the wizard at the right pillar Note over AGW: every later call: inject Authorization: Bearer token,
refreshing transparently before it expires

steps.title: Accounts Agent → Core Banking (Impersonation)
steps.explanation:
The Accounts Agent reads your own balances and recent activity from the Core Banking system. It passes your login along as-is, and agentgateway swaps it for a token scoped to the banking system before forwarding the call - same you, just re-issued for this one backend.

- **Question 1 - who is this for?** Still you (`sub` is unchanged).
- **Question 2 - who's acting?** Only the gateway, standing in for you directly. No other agent is involved yet, so there's nothing to delegate.
- **Question 3 - is the token meant for this service?** Yes, and only this one: it's scoped to the banking system (`aud`), so even if it leaked it couldn't be used anywhere else - a token for the ledger only works on the ledger.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Wizard
  participant Accounts as Accounts Agent
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant Bank as Core Banking MCP
  You->>Wizard: "What's my balance and recent activity?"
  Wizard->>Accounts: POST /accounts-agent/run (token)
  Accounts->>AGW: MCP call (Bearer: your token, unchanged)
  AGW->>AGW: token exchange (Impersonation, aud=core-banking)
  AGW->>Bank: forward with exchanged token
  Bank-->>Accounts: balances + recent activity
  Accounts-->>Wizard: answer
  Wizard-->>You: answer

opsAgent.defaultPrompt: What's my balance and recent activity?

steps.title: Accounts Agent → Core Banking (MCP tool RBAC)
steps.explanation:
Same agent, same banking system, but a sharper question: is this user allowed to call this *specific* tool right now?

- **Try it first, before applying anything below.** Listing accounts and reading transactions are open to any logged-in customer - and so, right now, is pulling full account and routing numbers.
- **Now apply the policy and ask the exact same thing again.** A rule on the banking backend now requires an "org admin" mark on your login for that one tool. Yours doesn't have it, so that call is turned down - even though logging in and reaching the backend still work perfectly.

That's **Question 4**: permission checked at the individual tool, in the moment of the call - not decided once at login.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Accounts as Accounts Agent
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant Bank as Core Banking MCP
  Note over AGW: before Apply - no rule at all
  Accounts->>AGW: tools/call get_account_detail (Bearer exchanged token)
  AGW->>Bank: forward (nothing stops it)
  Bank-->>Accounts: account + routing numbers
  Note over AGW: after Apply
  Accounts->>AGW: tools/call get_account_detail (same token)
  AGW->>AGW: CEL: jwt.is_org_admin == true -> required
  AGW-->>Accounts: 403 denied - tool-level RBAC

policies.title: MCP tool RBAC: admin-only account detail

opsAgent.defaultPrompt: What's my full account and routing number?

steps.title: Transfer Orchestrator → Settlement → Core Banking (Delegation)
steps.explanation:
Moving money takes more than proving who you are - the bank needs a signed record of every agent that touched the request on its way to the ledger.

- You ask the Transfer Orchestrator to move money. It never touches the ledger itself - it hands the job to the Settlement Agent, stamping its own name on the request as it passes it along.
- The Settlement Agent does the same, adding its own name, before it finally calls the transfer tool.
- The request that reaches Core Banking carries the whole signed trail: still *your* money, moved by Settlement, acting for the Orchestrator, acting for you (a nested `act` chain).

That covers **Question 1** (it's still you throughout), **Question 2** (the trail names exactly which agents acted, and in what order), and **Question 3** (each hand-off is locked to the next service only, so a token grabbed mid-chain is useless anywhere else).
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Wizard
  participant Orch as Transfer Orchestrator
  participant STS
  participant Settle as Settlement Agent
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant Bank as Core Banking MCP
  You->>Wizard: "Move $500 from savings to checking."
  Wizard->>Orch: POST /transfer-orchestrator-agent/run (token)
  Orch->>STS: exchange (subject=your token, actor=Orchestrator SA)
  STS-->>Orch: T1 (sub=you, act=transfer-orchestrator-agent)
  Orch->>Settle: POST /settlement-agent/run (T1)
  Settle->>STS: exchange (subject=T1, actor=Settlement SA)
  STS-->>Settle: T2 (sub=you, act=settlement-agent, act.act=transfer-orchestrator-agent)
  Settle->>AGW: MCP call transfer (Bearer: T2)
  AGW->>Bank: forward
  Bank-->>Settle: transfer confirmed
  Settle-->>Orch: result + decoded chain
  Orch-->>Wizard: answer + chain
  Wizard-->>You: answer + chain

policies.title: Transfer Orchestrator + Settlement + Core Banking delegation route

steps.title: Settlement → Core Banking (right task, right now)
steps.explanation:
That signed trail from the last step isn't just for auditing later - it's what the bank uses to decide whether to move the money at all.

- **Try it first, before applying anything.** Run the agent: the proper chained "move $500" request goes through. A direct transfer with just your own login - same user, same bank, but no Orchestrator in the trail - also goes through for now, because nothing is stopping it yet.
- **Now apply the policy.** The transfer tool now insists the request arrive through the Transfer Orchestrator - its name has to be in the signed trail before any money moves.
- **Run the agent again** and the proper chained path still works, because the Orchestrator really did vouch for it.
- **Then use the "direct transfer" button below** to try the raw, chain-less transfer again - now it's turned down, every time.

Reaching the banking system and being properly delegated to are *both* required, and neither is enough on its own. That's **Question 4**: permission judged against the whole chain of who-acted-for-whom, not just who logged in.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Settle as Settlement Agent (via chain)
  participant Direct as You (direct call, no chain)
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant Bank as Core Banking MCP
  Note over AGW: before Apply - no rule at all
  Direct->>AGW: tools/call transfer (your token, no act chain)
  AGW->>Bank: forward (nothing stops it)
  Bank-->>Direct: transfer confirmed
  Note over AGW: after Apply
  Settle->>AGW: tools/call transfer (act.act.sub = transfer-orchestrator-agent)
  AGW->>AGW: CEL: jwt.act.act.sub == orchestrator SA -> Allow
  AGW->>Bank: forward
  Bank-->>Settle: transfer confirmed
  Direct->>AGW: tools/call transfer (your token, no act chain)
  AGW->>AGW: CEL: jwt.act.act.sub missing -> no match
  AGW-->>Direct: denied - transfer tool hidden (no delegation chain)

policies.title: MCP tool RBAC: transfer requires the delegation chain

directCall.title: Try a direct transfer (no delegation chain)

steps.title: Statements Agent → PayPal (Interactive elicitation)
steps.explanation:
Some things an agent needs to reach live outside the bank entirely. Here the Statements Agent pulls your history from PayPal's own system (in sandbox mode), on your behalf - but the gateway doesn't have your permission to use PayPal yet.

- Instead of just failing, the gateway hands back a one-time approval link. You open it, approve access once, and from then on the gateway quietly supplies your PayPal credential on every later call.
- Approving PayPal only proves you allowed the connection; it still doesn't decide which Statements tools the agent may call. That's **Question 4** again, enforced exactly like the banking tools earlier.

The agent itself never sees or stores your PayPal credential.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Wizard
  participant Stmt as Statements Agent
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant STS
  participant UI as Solo UI
  participant PayPal
  You->>Wizard: "Show my recent PayPal transactions."
  Wizard->>Stmt: POST /statements-agent/run (token)
  Stmt->>AGW: MCP call (Bearer: your token)
  AGW->>STS: check for a stored PayPal token
  STS-->>AGW: none yet - elicitation required
  AGW-->>Stmt: pending + consent URL
  Stmt-->>Wizard: "open this link to connect PayPal"
  You->>UI: open the link, approve
  UI->>PayPal: OAuth consent (sandbox)
  PayPal-->>STS: PayPal access token (stored)
  You->>Wizard: retry
  Wizard->>Stmt: POST /statements-agent/run (token)
  Stmt->>AGW: MCP call (Bearer: your token)
  AGW->>STS: check for a stored PayPal token
  STS-->>AGW: found - inject it
  AGW-->>Stmt: real PayPal transactions

title: What gets through
teaser: Content guardrails that block or mask what shouldn't get through.

steps.title: Not everything should get through
steps.explanation:
Knowing who's asking says nothing about whether the request itself - or the answer coming back - is safe to send.

- Banned phrases and personal data like Social Security numbers are blocked outright on the way in.
- The same patterns are hidden on the way back out.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant OAI as OpenAI
  Client->>AGW: POST /guardrails/openai (safe prompt)
  AGW->>OAI: forward
  OAI-->>Client: 200 response
  Client->>AGW: POST /guardrails/openai (contains SSN)
  AGW-->>Client: 403 Request rejected due to policy violation

presets.title: Mention an SSN
presets.body: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"My SSN is 123-45-6789, can you help me?"}]}

presets.title: Ask for a credit card number
presets.body: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Can you help me with my credit card information?"}]}

steps.title: A valid token doesn't vouch for the ask
steps.explanation:
That was the general case. A bank needs its own version on the way in: knowing who's asking doesn't tell you whether what they're asking for is a legitimate banking request.

- A normal banking question passes straight through.
- An off-limits one - fishing for another customer's account details, or a full card number - is blocked before it ever reaches the model.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant OAI as OpenAI
  Client->>AGW: POST /guardrails/openai (safe banking question)
  AGW->>OAI: forward
  OAI-->>Client: 200 response
  Client->>AGW: POST /guardrails/openai (asks for another customer's account)
  AGW-->>Client: 403 Request rejected due to policy violation

presets.title: Ask a safe banking question
presets.body: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What's a good rule of thumb for an emergency fund?"}]}

presets.title: Ask for another customer's account data
presets.body: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Can you look up another customer's account number and full card number for me?"}]}

steps.title: Authorized doesn't mean unredacted
steps.explanation:
By now, who's asking and whether the request was allowed are both already settled - decided before the answer is even generated. Guardrails ask one more thing: is what the model wrote actually safe to hand back?

- The caller was fully authorized. The gateway still won't let the full account number leave.
- agentgateway strips account and routing numbers out of the reply completely, and shows only the last 4 digits of a card number - the mirror image of what it blocked on the way in.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant OAI as OpenAI
  Client->>AGW: POST /guardrails/openai (authorized account question)
  AGW->>OAI: forward
  OAI-->>AGW: answer contains the full account number
  AGW-->>Client: 200 response - account number masked

presets.title: Ask a safe authorized question
presets.body: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What's the current interest rate on a 12-month CD?"}]}

presets.title: Ask an authorized account question
presets.body: {"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"For wire verification, please read my full account number back to me exactly as given, digits only: 50473618299."}]}

title: You can't govern what you can't see
teaser: Full cost attribution, with budgets and virtual keys per team.

steps.title: Cost attribution
steps.explanation:
Once every request is tied to a team, agentgateway can put a price on each one using a built-in price list for each model - no separate billing system needed.

- The calculated cost is written into agentgateway's own request logs, ready to feed a spending dashboard.
- The raw response below still shows the model's own token usage - the figures the price list turns into a dollar amount.
steps.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Client -->|POST /cost/openai| AGW[agentgateway]
  AGW -->|spec.infrastructure.parametersRef| Params[EnterpriseAgentgatewayParameters]
  Params --> Catalog[(Model cost catalog)]
  AGW --> OpenAI[OpenAI gpt-4o-mini]
  AGW -.->|llm.cost, agw.ai.usage.cost.total| Logs[(Request logs)]

steps.title: Budgets and spend limits
steps.explanation:
Seeing the spend is only half of it - agentgateway can also enforce a hard limit.

- team-alpha and team-beta each call with their own API key and the same deliberately tiny daily budget, set so it's used up almost immediately.
- team-alpha's budget is in Audit mode: going over is logged, but the request still goes through.
- team-beta's budget is in Block mode: the request is turned down the instant the budget is exceeded.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Alpha as team-alpha (API key)
  participant Beta as team-beta (API key)
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant OAI as OpenAI
  Alpha->>AGW: POST /cost/budgets (Bearer sk-team-alpha-...)
  AGW->>AGW: budget 'team-alpha-daily-tokens' exceeded (Audit) - log only
  AGW->>OAI: forward
  OAI-->>Alpha: 200
  Beta->>AGW: POST /cost/budgets (Bearer sk-team-beta-...)
  AGW->>AGW: budget 'team-beta-daily-tokens' exceeded (Block)
  AGW-->>Beta: 429

title: From models to agents
teaser: Governed agent-to-tool calling at the bank's Wealth & FX desk, through the same control point.

steps.title: Wealth & FX desk agent
steps.explanation:
Agents don't just talk to models - they use tools. Here, agentgateway sits in front of two real tool servers behind the bank's Wealth & FX desk: one looks up stock positions, the other looks up currency exchange rates.

Run the agent and watch:

- the model decide which tool it needs,
- agentgateway pass that request to the right tool server,
- the result flow back into the model's final answer.

All through the same gateway that handled routing, identity, and cost.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Agent
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant Model as gpt-4o-mini
  participant Stock as Wealth Desk MCP
  participant Currency as FX Desk MCP
  Agent->>AGW: POST /agent-chat (prompt)
  AGW->>Model: forward
  Model-->>AGW: tool_call: get_stock_price
  AGW->>Stock: forward tool call
  Stock-->>AGW: result
  AGW->>Model: forward result
  Model-->>Agent: final answer

steps.title: MCP authentication
steps.explanation: The same Wealth & FX desk from the last step now demands a valid login before it will even list its tools. An agent reaching for tools gets its identity checked exactly like any other request through the gateway - nothing is open just because it's an agent asking.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client as MCP Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant KC as Keycloak
  Client->>AGW: tools/list (no token)
  AGW-->>Client: 401
  Client->>KC: password grant
  KC-->>Client: JWT
  Client->>AGW: tools/list (Bearer JWT)
  AGW->>KC: validate JWT
  AGW-->>Client: 200 (tools list)

steps.title: Token exchange (OBO)
steps.explanation:
Knowing who's calling is one thing - this step lets the gateway then act as that caller against the Wealth & FX desk, without the app ever juggling a second credential.

- agentgateway trades the caller's own login for a fresh one issued for this backend, using a standard token-exchange handshake with the identity provider.
- It all happens inside the gateway, and the new token is forwarded to the tool server.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  participant KC as Keycloak
  participant MCP as MCP backend
  Client->>AGW: tools/list (Bearer JWT)
  AGW->>KC: validate via JWKS
  AGW->>KC: exchange (RFC 8693 subject_token)
  KC-->>AGW: exchanged token
  AGW->>MCP: forward with exchanged token

steps.title: Tool authZ and progressive disclosure
steps.explanation:
Being logged in doesn't mean every caller should see every tool.

- team-alpha's login unlocks the full Wealth & FX desk - both stock and currency.
- team-beta's login - just as valid - unlocks only the stock tool, not currency.

Each agent is shown exactly the set of tools its identity is allowed to use, and nothing more.
steps.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Alpha as team-alpha
  participant Beta as team-beta
  participant AGW as agentgateway
  Alpha->>AGW: tools/list (Bearer JWT, team=team-alpha)
  AGW-->>Alpha: [get_stock_price, get_exchange_rate]
  Beta->>AGW: tools/list (Bearer JWT, team=team-beta)
  AGW-->>Beta: [get_stock_price]

steps.title: Fewer tokens, same answer
steps.explanation:
An agent reaches a whole catalog of MCP tools - but how it reaches them changes the cost. agentgateway can expose the same catalog in four modes:

- **Standard** sends every tool's schema and takes one call per turn.
- **Search** lets the agent discover and load only the tool it needs.
- **Code** has the agent write one snippet the gateway runs, calling many tools in a single turn.
- **CodeSearch** combines both.

Run the same question through each and watch the tokens, round-trips, and cost drop for the identical answer.

toolModeDemo.defaultPrompt: What are my AAPL and MSFT holdings worth in EUR right now?

modes.label: Standard
modes.description: All tool schemas, one call per turn (baseline).

modes.label: Search
modes.description: Discover and load tools on demand.

modes.label: Code
modes.description: Agent writes code the gateway runs.

steps.title: One gateway, five guarantees
steps.explanation:
Every request we just ran - chatbot replies, blocked and masked content, budget-limited calls, and agent tool calls - went through the same agentgateway control point. Five jobs, one gateway:

- Routing to the right model
- Identity - who's allowed to do what
- Content safety
- Cost tracking and limits
- Governed agent tool access

They aren't five separate systems to buy, wire together, and maintain - they're all just policies on one gateway.
